subject: Logging controls for NovaMed pilot — redaction & retention
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, privacy@novamed.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: logging & PII controls from today's discovery

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was helpful. I wanted to capture the items NovaMed's security/privacy team flagged so we can move to a scoped pilot. Key asks from our side: 

- Can Redwood provide an explicit list of fields you expect to capture in request/response logs by default (headers, body, query params)? We need to map against our PII inventory.
- What out-of-the-box redaction capabilities exist for:
  - trace/span IDs and cookies
  - Authorization headers and bearer tokens
  - Patient identifiers in JSON payloads (MRN, SSN equivalents)
- Minimum/maximum retention options for structured logs and request traces (we need retention down to 7 days for dev, 90 days for prod; possibility of ultra-short retention for sensitive endpoints).
- Data residency: ability to route logs to our US-only log storage and not replicate to EU.

I've attached our PII inventory (NovaMed_PII_Inventory.xlsx) so you can match fields. Can someone on your team propose an initial redaction profile and a sample config we could test during a 2-week pilot?

Also: we will likely need SOC 2 evidence of log access controls — please indicate where we can find the relevant artifacts.

Next step: if you can send a short implementation plan (what Redwood will do, what we need to do, and an MTWP for the pilot), we can get legal and infra to sign off. Ideally before EOD Mon (23 Nov).

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Director, Privacy & Compliance
NovaMed Health

Attachment: NovaMed_PII_Inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: logging & PII controls from today's discovery

Hi Anjali —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers up front, then an ask for a short sync if useful: 

- Default capture surface: by default Redwood captures request metadata (method, path, response code, latency), selected headers (Host, Content-Type) and a small sample of body for troubleshooting. We do NOT persist Authorization headers or full request bodies unless a customer opts in.
- Redaction capabilities: we have token-level redaction rules (regex and JSON path) that can remove or mask values at ingestion. We also support header-level suppression (e.g., drop Authorization) and trace ID hashing.
- Retention windows: configurable per-route with policy tiers. We can do 7d/30d/90d and a 0d (ephemeral) option for sensitive endpoints.
- Residency: routing rules allow logs to be stored in a single region; for your pilot we can ensure logs remain in US regions and don't replicate to EU.

I'm attaching a short overview of the options (redaction-options.pdf) and our proposed pilot template. Can Karthik take point on the technical config and a sample ingestion policy?

If it helps, let's schedule a 30-min technical runbook review early next week. Ben will lead the commercial/contract work.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redaction-options.pdf (one-page PDF)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali.rao@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: logging & PII controls from today's discovery

Anjali / team —

Quick technical sketch of how we'd approach the pilot. This is intentionally concise; happy to expand in the runbook call: 

1) Ingestion profile (route-level)
- Create a dedicated route for NovaMed pilot traffic: /api/novamed/*
- Ingestion policy: drop headers named Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie at the ingest proxy.
- JSON path redaction rules: remove fields $.patient.mrn, $.patient.ssn, mask $.patient.name with first-letter-only rule.
- Trace IDs: apply one-way hash at edge (sha256) before persisting; store unhashed only in ephemeral cache (30s) for debugging.

2) Retention & storage
- Set pilot retention to 14 days for dev and 90 days for a narrow production subset. We can mark specific log streams as "ephemeral" for 0-day retention.

3) Residency
- Route archived logs to your US-only S3 bucket (no cross-region replication). We will provide an IAM role and a presigned upload flow.

4) Access & audit
- Role-based access controls: only an approved list of Redwood operators and your security contacts will have read access; all reads are logged (audit trail).

Sample config (ingestion rule snippet):
```
route: /api/novamed/*
redaction:
  headers_drop: ["Authorization","Cookie","Set-Cookie"]
  json_paths_mask: ["$.patient.mrn","$.patient.ssn"]
  json_paths_partial_mask: [{"path":"$.patient.name","rule":"first-char"}]
retention: 14d
residency: us-east-1
```
I'll create a playbook document and send it to you (log-redaction-playbook.md) with operational runbooks and rollback steps. Could you confirm the test endpoints and whether you want hashed trace IDs correlated to your internal tracing (we can add mapping but it requires a short-lived shared key)?

-Karthik

Attachment: log-redaction-playbook.md (playbook stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Anjali —

Thanks for the details and for sharing the inventory. Per Marissa and Karthik below, here's a short mutual action plan to get the pilot kicked off: 

1) Week of Nov 29 — Kickoff & config lock
   - Redwood: provide pilot ingestion policy and sample config (Karthik).
   - NovaMed: supply 3 test endpoints and a staging API key.
2) Dec 6 — Pilot deploy (2 weeks)
   - Redwood: deploy redaction rules, route logs to your US bucket, enable ephemeral retention for sensitive streams.
   - NovaMed: run synthetic traffic + 2 smoke tests.
3) Dec 20 — Review & sign-off
   - Joint review of logs, compliance checklist, and SOC 2 artifacts. Decide on production retention and routing.

Action items for this email thread:
- Anjali: confirm test endpoints and the staging key owner (reply here).
- Marissa: please drop the pilot ingestion policy link in the thread (Karthik, when ready).
- Ben: I'll prepare a standard pilot addendum and attach to HubSpot (deal HS-55421).

We can also add a short statement in the addendum about trace ID hashing and the optional mapping key. If you prefer, I can loop in Legal/Procurement once you confirm the timeline.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
